issue: Must a continuing criminal enterprise (CCE) indictment allege facts identifying the three predicate offenses, or is citing the violated statutory provisions for those predicate offenses sufficient?
provision: 21 U.S.C. § 848; U.S. Const. amend. V (grand jury indictment requirement)

sides.position: A CCE count is constitutionally sufficient if it identifies the predicate violations by reference to the violated statutory provisions, without describing their factual content.
cases: United States v. Montague, 67 F.4th 529 (2d Cir. 2023)
United States v. Flaharty, 295 F.3d 182 (2d Cir. 2002)
United States v. Montague, 84 F.4th 533 (2d Cir. 2023)

sides.position: An indictment must include the facts and circumstances comprising at least three predicate offenses, though the CCE count need not specify which three will ultimately prove the charge.
cases: United States v. Bansal, 663 F.3d 634 (3d Cir. 2011)

quote: There can be no doubt of the circuit split here: the panel majority twice rejects Bansal by name.
cite: United States v. Montague, 84 F.4th 533 (2d Cir. 2023)
